run.question:
Customers reported slow checkout for the last hour. Check our Datadog APM
traces for the checkout-service and find which downstream call is slow.

report.summary: The requested source, Datadog APM, is not configured for this Run: the available integrations are Jaeger, Prometheus, Elasticsearch and Kubernetes (only change_history is listed as not integrated), so no Datadog traces could be queried. The trace backend that is available, Jaeger, returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE on every attempt (traces_list_services, traces_list_operations, traces_search, traces_search_by_tags), as did every Prometheus query (metrics_range_query, execute_prometheus_instant_query, get_metric_names, get_label_values, get_prometheus_target), so no checkout span or per-dependency latency could be read; the Elasticsearch index listing returned no indices. Consequently the slow downstream call could not be identified from traces, and no root cause is asserted. What could be observed on the cluster (queried at ~17:50 UTC on 2026-11-23, namespace otel-demo) shows checkout itself healthy: Deployment checkout 1/1 ready created 2026-11-23T14:36:29Z, pod checkout-6578865d87-v6flf Running/ready with 0 restarts, and every order logged by that pod between 16:50:53 and 17:49:51 completed its PlaceOrder → payment → email steps in roughly 10–40 ms with no error lines. Payment's own log shows charge handling in about 1–2 ms. All flagd fault-injection flags (paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, cartFailure, productCatalogFailure, etc.) had defaultVariant "off" at query time. The only anomaly seen was in the telemetry pipeline: otel-collector logged repeated 'failed to upload metrics ... code = Unavailable ... otel-collector:4318' errors every ~10 s through the window, which is a plausible explanation for missing metric data but does not by itself show which downstream call is slow, and the customer-reported slowness remains unverified. Note also that a Kubernetes Service named checkout exists in otel-demo, while no service named checkout-service was returned.

claims.text: Deployment checkout in namespace otel-demo reported 1 desired / 1 available / 1 ready / 1 updated replica at query time (17:50 UTC, 2026-11-23).
Pod checkout-6578865d87-v6flf (namespace otel-demo, owner ReplicaSet checkout-6578865d87) was Running, all containers ready, restart count 0 at query time.

The Kubernetes Service inventory of namespace otel-demo contains a ClusterIP Service named checkout (selector opentelemetry.io/name=checkout) and no Service named checkout-service among the 26 returned entries.

Checkout pod logs between 16:50:53 and 17:19:38 show complete order sequences: for example 17:19:38.598119 PlaceOrder → 17:19:38.616238 'payment went through' → 17:19:38.625342 'order confirmation email sent', i.e. the steps finish within ~27 ms of each other.

Checkout pod logs between 17:27:10 and 17:49:51 continue to show the same pattern with no error severity: e.g. 17:49:51.171939 PlaceOrder → 17:49:51.190379 payment → 17:49:51.200708 email confirmation.

Payment pod payment-6f7bc865d6-wwqnm logged 'Charge request received' at 17:47:08.124044 and 'Transaction complete' at 17:47:08.125686 for the same trace_id (826706594c39340529bf41ab31acdb6b), about 1.6 ms apart, with level info.

ConfigMap flagd-config (otel-demo) had every fault/latency flag with defaultVariant "off" at query time, including paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, cartFailure, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, adFailure, adHighCpu, adManualGc, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage and imageSlowLoad.

Pod otel-collector-69c9f9649-vdpcn logged repeated failures in the window: 'failed to upload metrics: reader collect and export timeout: rpc error: code = Unavailable ... error reading server preface: http2 ...' every ~10 seconds from 17:45:48 through 17:50:18, plus grpc client warnings connecting to Addr 10.96.73.1:4318, ServerName "otel-collector:4318".

The same otel-collector pod's debug exporter logged continuous trace batches being received just before query time (e.g. 23 spans at 17:49:54.091, 12 spans at 17:50:15.168), so trace ingest into the collector was active in the window.

The checkout and payment application logs that could be read do not show a slow downstream step: 285 checkout lines in the hour (three per order) and the sampled orders all complete PlaceOrder→payment→email within tens of milliseconds with info severity only; this is evidence against any of cart, product-catalog, currency, shipping quote, payment or email being slow on the sampled requests.

The failure to obtain any trace or metric data may be connected to the otel-collector's continuous metric-export failures to otel-collector:4318 in the same window, but that would explain missing telemetry, not the slow checkout itself; no evidence ties it to a particular downstream call.

A candidate downstream dependency of checkout remains unresolved rather than identified: cart, product-catalog, currency, shipping (quote), payment and email all exist as ClusterIP Services in otel-demo, but no span-duration or error-rate reading for any of them was obtainable in this Run, so none can be named as the slow call.

A flagd-injected fault on checkout's dependencies is not supported for the current state: every failure/latency flag in ConfigMap flagd-config was set to defaultVariant "off", and no pod showed restarts or OOM/Evicted marks.

Restore or authorise the trace backend (Datadog APM, or the Jaeger/Prometheus target that returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE) and then rank checkout's client spans by p99 duration — e.g. rpc_client_duration_milliseconds by rpc_service/rpc_method for service_name=checkout, or span durations for the checkout operations — before naming the slow downstream call.

gaps: Datadog APM is not one of the data sources available in this Run (available: elasticsearch, jaeger, kubernetes, prometheus), so no Datadog trace for checkout-service could be queried at all.

Jaeger returned status error / SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE (target m0-otel-20260909) for traces_list_services and traces_list_operations at 17:50:23, for traces_search at 17:50:25, 17:50:28, 17:51:27 and 17:51:27, and for traces_search_by_tags at 17:50:49 — therefore no span, operation, status or duration evidence for checkout or any downstream service exists for the last hour, and the exact Jaeger service naming (checkout vs checkout-service) could not be confirmed.

Prometheus queries also returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE (get_metric_names 17:50:25, execute_prometheus_instant_query 17:50:28, get_prometheus_target 17:50:32, metrics_range_query 17:50:32 and 17:50:42, get_label_values 17:50:49), so traces_span_metrics_calls_total, rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_* and http_server_request_duration_seconds_count could not be read; the absence of latency readings is unknown, not zero.
Elasticsearch index listing (pattern *) returned no indices, so no log search was possible; log evidence was limited to pod stdout via the Kubernetes API.

The cluster events listing across all namespaces returned no events inside the authorised window, so no event-based signal (kubelet eviction, OOM, rollout) is available; this is unobserved, not proof nothing occurred.

Checkout logs contain only three lines per order (PlaceOrder, payment went through, email sent) and no per-dependency timing or error lines; the slow call, if it exists, is not recorded there, and log lines beyond the 4 MiB read limit / omitted lines were not examined.
Whether customers actually experienced slow checkout in the last hour is unverified: no latency metric, SLO or trace duration was obtainable.
No change history integration is configured (change_history listed as not integrated), so no deployment/configuration change record for the window could be checked.
next_steps: Provide or authorise access to the trace backend actually holding checkout spans (Datadog APM, or fix the Jaeger/Prometheus target reachability), then compare p99 client-span durations per downstream operation for checkout over 16:50–17:50 UTC against an earlier comparable baseline.
Investigate why otel-collector's metric uploads to otel-collector:4318 fail with gRPC Unavailable/http2 preface errors, since that blocks metric series that would show which dependency degraded.

Once span data is available, check cart (valkey-cart), product-catalog, currency, shipping/quote, payment and email client spans from checkout individually before attributing the slowdown to any one of them.

Confirm with a load/trace capture whether the checkout HTTP endpoint (or the frontend checkout page) is slow, since the checkout application logs show each sampled order completing in tens of milliseconds.
